findings.title: Interpolation now happens twice
findings.body: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on each query target before splitting, but runSplitGroupedQueries subsequently constructs subRequest objects that are passed to datasource.runQuery, which internally (per Loki datasource logic) typically also applies template variable interpolation per sub-request (e.g. with per-chunk scopedVars/range). Since runSplitQuery is also called from shardQuerySplitting.ts via runSplitQuery after shardQuerySplitting already applied applyTemplateVariables itself, templates variables may be interpolated twice. If applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent (e.g. replaces $__range or special chars) this can corrupt the final query text, especially for shard splitting flows where interpolation happens for both the sharding step and inside runSplitQuery.

findings.title: scopedVars/range not updated per split sub-request
findings.body: Interpolation is now done once up-front at the full request's range/scopedVars, before time-range splitting occurs. Any template variables that depend on the per-chunk time range (e.g. $__range, $__interval relative to the sub-request's partitioned range) will be resolved using the original, unsplit request range rather than each sub-request's actual range. This changes behavior from before, where (seemingly) interpolation happened closer to execution. This could silently produce incorrect query results for queries using range-dependent variables within split sub-queries, though isQueryWithRangeVariable queries are excluded from splitting, other interval-based vars like $__interval may still be affected per chunk since runQuery normally recomputes them for each subRequest with its own range/intervalMs — but now the interpolation already happened on the original query before this per-chunk recompute could take effect, defeating per-chunk accuracy for $__interval and similar vars.

findings.title: Possible double interpolation across shardQuerySplitting -> runSplitQuery
findings.body: shardQuerySplitting.ts now applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables to each target instead of the previous interpolateVariablesInQueries. Downstream, splitQueriesByStreamShard calls runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts) with these already-interpolated queries, where runSplitQuery itself calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on request.targets again. If applyTemplateVariables isn't idempotent for all variable types (e.g., special characters introduced by shard selector string manipulation such as __stream_shard__=~"20|10"), the second interpolation pass could mangle the already-built shard selector expression.
